Adri
San Jose, Costa Rica279 contributions

Definitly no-no for "fusion" food
Jan 2019 • Family
10 days in Vietnam we asked our tour guide for a different place for lunch. She looked and took us here which its vietnamite-fusion food. 
Staff barely speaks english. 
3 main dishes at a higher price than any other place: honey glazed chicken (bad), steak on mushroom sauce just ok, filet mignon with green pepper sauce (fortunately sauce on the side since tasted like plastic). Meat not cooked as order and without much flavor. 
Sides for everyplate: 2 cherry tomatoes (just like that), little bunch of fries. 
We ordered crepe flambè with ice cream: saw our waiter do it 10 mts away from us when was supossed to be made at the table. Dought was "goewy" (regular vainilla ice cream). 
3 sodas, 3 main and 1 dessert 1.042.000 VND (high for Vietnam standars). 
The place seems to be a spot for tour companies since we saw 2 groups previously meet at Cu Chi tunnels, the all had a set menu beautifully decor (vietnamite food), so can comment on that part of the menu.

London, United Kingdom12 contributions

Romantic setting
Oct 2013 • Couples
I chose this restaurant as I wanted to take my wife to a new venue to commemorate our anniversary and wasn't disappointed. A basket of flowers (orchids and roses) and lovely message got us off to a great start. The staff were dressed in a way (tuxedos) that very-much complemented the attempted ambience and perhaps the best feature was the duet by the 2 musicians. The violin and cello were really spot on in terms of volume and choice of music.
I would personally rate the food and value as "Good" as opposed to "Average" or "Very Good", my main critique was that the bread roll could have been fresher...either soft, delicious bread or nothing at all is my view.
Other than that, we had a lovely evening and would recommend as one of the better restaurants if it's the romantic feeling you're after.

Not a fine dining
Oct 2013 • Couples
We were very disappointed! This place advertised as a fine dining and it wasn't. Well, may be they're trying...but they need to learn a lot more. Waiters dress in tuxedos but didn't know how to do their jobs! They just standing there and looking at each others, finally I could not stand it anymore I told the maître d'hotel that it's so noisy in here, he acted like there's nothing he can do. Now come the desert, I ordered a Flan (egg custard) and he brought me a big soup spoon for my tiny Flan (?!), I had to asked him to give me another small spoon so I can have my flan. Is this really a fine dining? Absolutely not! Food was mediocre, atmosphere was lousy and the service team didn't really know how to do their job! For a fine dining as they advertised, that was unacceptable! Never come back!

A restaurant with heart
Aug 2013 • Couples
I don't normally write reviews for restaurants. One because I like reviewing hotels more and I think when it comes to travelling, a good hotel is of utmost importance. Two because my partner is an experienced food connoisseur who writes local restaurant reviews frequently and so I prefer leaving the food reviews to her. However, after visiting Le Chateau de Saigon, she said to me, "I think you should write a review on TripAdvisor; perhaps that can help boost its ratings a bit." 
The reason she said so is because we both agree this place deserves a higher placing on TripAdvisor's HCMC restaurant list. Yes it's French cuisine may not be top notch e.g. the Grand Marnier Soufflé looked and tasted a bit more like pudding than the normal soufflé we know of, but it is a restaurant with a lot of heart. You can feel that from the moment you enter the place. The waiters were all well dressed in tidy tuxedos and greeted guests warmly, and you could also feel that lots of effort were put into serving the diners.
As for the food, quality and taste were very reasonable given its price. Wine, however, was not particularly cheap and it is up there with any one of the fine restaurants we have here in Hong Kong.
But all in all, we had a great experience at Le Chateau, and I hope more tourists get to discover this gem in Saigon.
